answer:
Accounting: on this machine each head moves one cell per step, so one linear pass over an array costs time proportional to its stored bits. The main result's input has V = Theta(n) stored bits, so one pass costs Theta(n). The layered transform (Divogam) has Theta(log n) layers. If each layer is one full pass over the data, the total is Theta(n) times Theta(log n), which is Theta(n log n), the bound to be beaten. To beat it, the work per layer must fall below one full pass. The wiki's route does this for both parts of a layer. Moving address bits so that paired entries sit together is a chunk interchange, which costs O(V u^tau) with tau < 1 (Fizokid). The butterfly arithmetic of several axes at once costs O(V d^lambda') with lambda' < 1, and runs as one sifigeg instead of one pass per axis (Sifigeg, Makevif). The Dedapov page then sums these cost terms, each a power of the width below one, and gets O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)).

Why only these two: the Bitebid page states that beating the bound needs cheaper address movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic. None of the pages I opened argues that other changes, such as fewer layers or a different radix, cannot also reduce the cost per layer. I accept the 'only' clause on the wiki's word, so that part of the answer is not established by the pages.

citations.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ divogam therefore already costs $\Theta(n)\cdot\Theta(\log n)=\Theta(n\log n)$, the bound to be beaten.
The data of the $n$-bit inputs occupy $V=\Theta(n)$ stored bits, so one pass costs $\Theta(n)$.
Repeated over the address bits of an array, with twiddle multiplications between layers, it computes the [Tobifup](kur) of an array in $\log_2 t$ layers instead of $t^2$ operations.
Beating that needs cheaper address movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic
in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time on fixed tapes, where $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ is the saving exponent
The tape layout arranges the address bits so that each round of a [libakur](gip) runs as one [sifigeg](tiz) instead of one pass per axis.

key_idea.statement: On a fixed-tape machine a linear pass over the array costs time proportional to its stored bits, so a layered transform that scans once per layer costs n log n, and any saving must make the work per layer cheaper than a full pass.
key_idea.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ divogam therefore already costs $\Theta(n)\cdot\Theta(\log n)=\Theta(n\log n)$, the bound to be beaten. So each rearrangement must cost one pass, not one pass per level.

stuck.quote: Beating that needs cheaper address movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic
stuck.note: The page asserts that only cheaper address movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic can beat the bound. No page I opened argues that other changes, such as fewer layers or another radix, cannot also cut the cost per layer. I could not tell whether this is a claim or a consequence.

stuck.quote: So each rearrangement must cost one pass, not one pass per level.
stuck.note: I followed that each layer costs a full pass, but not why the way below n log n is to make the per-layer cost sublinear, rather than to reduce the number of layers.

The page gives the recursion F(e) <= (s/W) F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau + 1) and says the leaves and log d pieces give O(d^lambda'). I could not rebuild from this how a round over d axes comes to d^lambda' rather than d passes.

stuck.quote: The recursion gets its strict inequality $s<Wm$ from [Pukezad](dol)
stuck.note: The inequality s < Wm that makes the geometric sum shrink is taken from the Pukezad page, which I did not open within my page budget. I accepted it on the page's word.

stuck.quote: The exponent is only $2^{-182}$ below one because $g_2$ multiplies three small numbers
stuck.note: I could follow the product 2^-75 times 2^-56 times 2^-50, but not why the chunk-exchange term, rather than the others, is the one that sets the saving. That link is what the question needs between address movement and the result.

stuck.quote: A simultaneous layer needs a round's selected bits at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.
stuck.note: The page requires the selected bits of each round to be regrouped at a common offset in consecutive chunks, and then does the regrouping. I followed the regrouping steps, but not why this grouping is what lets one round cost one pass.
I could not decode the term Tobifup. From this page I know only that the layers compute it. I did not open its page, so I do not know what it is.

reason: I am confident in the accounting: a full pass costs Theta(n) (Legafod) and there are Theta(log n) layers, giving Theta(n log n). I am also confident in how the two parts are made sublinear (Fizokid for chunk interchange, Sifigeg and Makevif for simultaneous rounds). I am not confident in the 'only' clause of the question. The Bitebid page asserts it without argument, and I found no argument excluding other tweaks. Several steps rest on pages I did not open (Pukezad, and the page for Tobifup), taken on the wiki's word. I opened 11 of the 15 allowed pages.
